---
title: "Contributing"
---

## Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/phpstats/juphyter
cd juphyter
composer install
```

`bin/juphyter` runs the checkout. `bin/juphyter install --name juphyter-dev`
registers a kernel that runs it, without replacing the `php` kernel.

## Tests

The PHP tests and the coding standard:

```bash
vendor/bin/pest
composer lint
```

A few tests send the engine an interrupt and are skipped when PHP lacks the
`pcntl` or `posix` extension. CI runs the PHP tests on PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5,
on Ubuntu and macOS.

The protocol tests start the kernel and drive it over the Jupyter protocol.
They need a Python with Jupyter:

```bash
python -m pip install -r tests/Protocol/requirements.txt
python -m pytest tests/Protocol
```

The render tests run Quarto on the documents in `tests/Quarto/fixture`. They
need Quarto, PHP 8.5, and a Python with the packages in
`tests/Quarto/requirements.txt`, and they install phibble, phplyr, and phiz
from `tests/Quarto/fixture/composer.json` into `build/`:

```bash
python -m pip install -r tests/Quarto/requirements.txt
python -m pytest tests/Quarto
```

`.github/workflows/family.yml` runs the display formatter tests with phibble,
phplyr, and phiz installed. None of the three is a dependency of juphyter.

## Documentation

The documentation is a Quarto site in `docs/`, and most pages run their PHP
cells through the kernel. phpstats.org imports the rendered HTML from this
repository and does not run Quarto, so the rendered pages and the frozen
output under `docs/_freeze/` are committed with their sources.

```bash
scripts/render-docs
```

The script installs phibble, phplyr, and phiz into `build/docs/sandbox` from
the render tests' manifest, registers a `php` kernel in a private Jupyter data
directory under `build/docs`, renders every page through it, and copies the
result into `docs/`. It needs PHP 8.5, because the overview uses the pipe
operator. `--refresh` reinstalls the sandbox and the kernel. `scripts/render-docs
--help` lists the environment variables that choose the PHP and the Python.

An executing render changes the committed HTML and frozen output even when no
source changed, because Quarto gives each executed cell a new random id.

```bash
scripts/render-docs --frozen
```

renders from the frozen output with no PHP. Quarto looks up each page's
kernel by name before it reads frozen output, so the script registers a `php`
kernel whose command exits immediately, and a page that needs executing fails
the render. CI uses this to check that the committed HTML matches the
sources.

A page joins the site through the `sidebar` in `docs/_quarto.yml`.
phpstats.org takes its navigation from that sidebar and fails to sync a page
that is listed without rendered HTML. `site/site.json` holds the install
commands, requirements, and summary that phpstats.org shows on the package's
overview.

Plans and design notes are kept in `docs/work/`, outside the site.

## The PHAR

```bash
php scripts/build-phar.php
```

writes `build/juphyter.phar` from the files listed in `phar.json`. `php
juphyter.phar install` registers a kernel whose engine is the PHAR, and copies
the Python transport beside the kernelspec, because Python cannot import from
inside a PHAR. No PHAR is published with a release.
